  `scrollToIndex(0)` after a re-sort to go back to the start. Positions are read from the rendered
  rows, so an array changed in place (`splice`, `sort`) and passed again still anchors correctly. The
  scroll container gets `overflow-anchor: none`: the list, not the browser, keeps the position; the
  browser's own scroll anchoring can move `scrollTop` while the list renders and leave a blank area.
- The first render waits for layout: if `clientHeight` is 0 (not yet in `document`) it is retried
  in `onMounted`. In jsdom tests fake `clientHeight`/`scrollTop` with `Object.defineProperty` and
  dispatch `new Event('scroll')` (see `packages/tests/src/components/virtualization.test.ts`).
- `refresh()` reloads page 0 through `dataRequest` and disposes every cached row (returns a
  `Promise`); `setData(items)` replaces the data without a request (`hasMore` becomes `false`, rows of items that
  stay are kept);
  `updateHeights()` rereads every height and renders the window when heights change while the data
  stays the same (rows kept, `filter` not rerun, nothing requested, the top visible row keeps its
  place); `scrollToIndex(i)` scrolls and renders synchronously; `getState()` returns a shallow copy of
  the state.
- A row that leaves the window receives `onDeactivated`; a cached row coming back receives
  `onActivated`.
- Paged mode: the scrollbar represents **loaded** pages only (the loaded rows after `filter` x row height), giving an
  infinite-scroll feel; it grows as pages arrive.

## Placement rule for `content`

Both forms place the rows component inside `mainTemplate`:

- `<content></content>`: the compiler turns **any** lowercase tag name that is not an HTML/SVG tag name
  into a variable reference, whether or not such a variable exists (an undeclared name fails at runtime),
  and a component instance is placed as is. Trap: a parameter named like an HTML tag (`header`, `main`,
  `section`, `slot`) produces that DOM element instead; keep the name `content` or another non-HTML name.
  A name with `-` stays a custom element.
- `{content}`: a bare identifier or member expression child is checked once, when the child is created: if
  it holds a component (or a non-empty array of components) it is placed; any other value becomes a
  text binding.

---

<!-- references/mobile-and-electron.md -->

# Phone-style apps and Electron / `file:` apps

MotifJS has no Electron- or Capacitor-specific API. What it offers for these targets is router
behaviour (`stack`, swipe-back, hash routing, `scrollMemory`, `keepAlive`), app lifecycle events and a
runtime that needs no `eval`. Full router reference: routing.md.

## Page stack (`useRouter({ stack })`)

```ts
app.useRouter({
  routes,
  stack: { retain: true, depth: 5, animation: 'slide', duration: 300, swipeBack: { edge: 24, threshold: 0.35 } },
});
```

| Option | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `stack` | off | `true` = all defaults. Leaving a page keeps its instance for back/forward instead of disposing it. Ignored in `mode: 'shell'`. |
| `retain` | `false` | `true`: kept pages stay in the DOM, hidden (`display:none !important` + `inert` + `aria-hidden`); `false`: detached, kept in memory. |
| `depth` | `5` | max kept previous pages; the oldest is disposed. |
| `persist` | `false` | write the stack's URIs to `sessionStorage`. |
| `animation` | `'none'` | `'slide'` or `async ({ direction, entering, leaving }) => void`; runs only for `push`/`back`/`forward`; skipped under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. |
| `duration` | `300` | ms, for `'slide'` and the swipe settle (60 % of it). |
| `swipeBack` | off | `true` or `{ edge = 24, threshold = 0.35 }`. |

Swipe-back: only a single touch that starts within `edge` px of the left edge, on a page that has a
previous entry, installs a (non-passive) move listener. Once the finger has moved 8 px mostly to the
right the page follows it and scrolling is prevented; a vertical or leftward move lets the touch go.
Releasing past `threshold` of the page width, or a rightward flick faster than 0.5 px/ms, calls
`history.back()`; otherwise the page snaps back. With `retain: true` the previous page is shown
underneath while dragging. A swipe-back navigation plays no page transitions.

`data-nav-direction`: with `stack`, whenever the stack animation does not run (no `animation`, or a
`initial`/`replace`/`traverse` navigation), the page's own transition (`transition` /
`motif.options.transition`) is the stack transition, and while it runs the page element carries
`data-nav-direction` (`initial` | `push` | `back` | `forward` | `replace` | `traverse`):

```css
[data-nav-direction="back"].page-enter-active { animation: slide-from-left .25s; }
[data-nav-direction="push"].page-enter-active { animation: slide-from-right .25s; }
```

`keepAlive: true` on a route keeps that route's instance across navigations (with or without `stack`);
it is detached, not disposed, and receives `onDeactivated` / `onActivated` (routing.md, lifecycle-and-dispose.md).

## App lifecycle (`app.onLifecycle`)

```ts
const off = app.onLifecycle(({ state }) => {
  if (state === 'resumed' || state === 'online') store.refresh();
});
```

| `state` | Source event |
|---|---|
| `'visible'` / `'hidden'` | `document` `visibilitychange` |
| `'frozen'` / `'resumed'` | `document` `freeze` / `resume` |
| `'restored'` | `window` `pageshow` with `persisted` (back/forward cache) |
| `'online'` / `'offline'` | `window` `online` / `offline` |

The handler receives `{ state, visible, online }`; `app.isVisible` and `app.isOnline` read the same
values at any time. The DOM listeners are installed on the first `onLifecycle` call and removed by
`app.dispose()`. The returned function unsubscribes. `onLifecycle` is **not** auto-disposed, not even
through `this.context`; in a component write
`this.motif.setDisposable(this.context.onLifecycle(fn))`.

## `file:` pages (Electron `loadFile`, packaged apps)

- Without `mode`, a page whose `location.protocol` is `file:` routes by the hash (`#/orders/5`), like
  `mode: 'hash'`; `'file'` is an explicit name for the same behaviour. Do not set `mode: 'history'` there:
  it reads `location.pathname`, which is the file path.
- `mode: 'shell'` never reads or writes the address bar or history and always starts at `/`; browser
  back/forward does not move it, and `stack` is ignored.
- The router stamps its own history entries (`history.state.__motifHistory`); when a back/forward
  navigation is cancelled (guard, `onLeave`, middleware) it moves the history back with `history.go()`
  so the address matches the page on screen. Calling `history.pushState` directly can skew that index.
- The runtime (`@motifx/core`) contains no `eval` / `new Function`, so a CSP without `'unsafe-eval'`
  works for MotifJS itself; JSX is compiled at build time. Third-party bundles have their own needs.

## Scroll and viewport

- `scrollMemory` (off by default) restores the scroll position per path on back/forward and link; the
  positions live in memory (kept across `restartRouter()`, lost on reload — save them with
  `app.router.saveScrollPositions(fn)` and put them back with `restoreScrollPositions`); `container`
  targets an inner scroller instead of the window. When on,
  `history.scrollRestoration` is `'manual'`. Options in routing.md.
- `stack` restores the inner scroll positions of a kept page when it returns.
- `Virtualization` re-renders its window when its scroll container's height changes (rotation,
  on-screen keyboard) through a `ResizeObserver` (virtualization.md).
- `Lazy` `retry: { count, delayMs, whenOnline = true }` retries a failed load; while the browser is
  offline it waits for the `online` event first (routing.md).

---

<!-- references/windows.md -->

# Windows: `app.windows`

A component can move into another same-origin window without being rebuilt: its object, state, bindings,
services and events stay in the page's JavaScript world; only the elements go. `app.windows` owns these
windows. Reach it as `this.context.windows` in a class or Options component, `useApplication().windows` in
a function component, `Application.main.windows` elsewhere.

## Opening

```ts
const win = await this.context.windows.open(editor, { width: 720, height: 560, title: 'Note' });   // popup
const top = await this.context.windows.open(editor, { kind: 'pip', width: 480, height: 360 });     // always-on-top
const empty = await this.context.windows.create({ width: 400, height: 300 }); empty.add(a, b);
const mine = this.context.windows.attach(iframe.contentWindow, { styles: 'once' });               // a window you already have
```

Call `open` / `create` inside a user gesture (a click handler): the browser call happens synchronously
and the promise resolves once the content is placed. `open(c, o)` is `create(o)` + `add(c)`.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `'popup'` (default) or `'pip'` (Document Picture-in-Picture: Chromium only, needs a gesture, one per page). |
| `fallback` | What to do when `pip` is missing or refused: `'popup'` (default) or `'none'` → rejects with `MJX419`. |
| `width`, `height`, `left`, `top` | Window size and position. |
| `name` | `window.open` name; unique per window when omitted. In Electron this is the `frameName` the main process sees. |
| `features` | Extra `window.open` feature string parts. |
| `title` | Window title; defaults to the page title. |
| `styles` | `'live'` (default), `'once'`, `'none'` or `(doc) => void`. |
| `orphans` | Content whose origin is gone when the window closes: `'dispose'` (default) or `'keep'`. |
| `closeWhenEmpty` | Close when the last component is disposed (default `true`). |
| `closeOnNavigate` | Close on every route change (default `false`). |
| `returnOnClose` | Put content back to its origin on close (default `true`); `false` sends components with an origin through `orphans` too. |
| `owner` | The window is registered in this component's dispose layer and closes with it. |
| `onClosing` | `(e: { window, components, reason }) => void`, called right before the window is torn down, content still inside. See Closing. |

## The handle (`AppWindow`)

`window`, `document`, `host` (the component wrapping the window body), `kind` (`'popup' | 'pip' | 'attached'`,
what really opened), `components`, `isOpen`, `add(...c)`, `release(c)` (back to its origin, window stays open),
`focus()`, `close()` → `{ returned, disposed, kept }`, `closed` (the same promise however the window closes),
`syncStyles()`. A toast or dialog opened by a component in the window belongs in that window:
`this.context.layerOf(this, dialog)` adds it to the window's `host` when the component's element is in a managed
window, to `app.layer` (the page layer, a plain `div` at the end of `body`) otherwise. Content placed in the
`host` this way is not in `win.components`: `orphans` and `returnOnClose` do not apply to it, it is disposed
with the window and appears in no list of the close result; content that must outlive the window goes through
`win.add` or a `Transport` slot.

## Origin and return

The first time a component is taken, the manager remembers its page parent and the sibling after it. The
component gets `onDeactivated`, enters the window host through `controls.add` and gets `onActivated`; `onMounted`
does not fire again (it fires in the window's own task queue when it never fired before). Moving between
windows keeps the origin. `release` and closing put the component back before the remembered sibling (or
that sibling's own remembered sibling when it is in a window too), else at the end. `returnOnClose: false` turns
this off (`release` still returns). No origin left → `orphans`:
dispose (default) or keep detached (`closed.kept`). Only a component given through `open` or `add` has an origin:
what the app moves into an attached window on its own is unknown to the manager, nothing is returned for it on
close and `components` does not list it.

## Closing

User close, `win.close()` or the window's `pagehide` → content returns, `closed` resolves. A component disposed
by the app drops out of the window; an empty window closes unless `closeWhenEmpty: false`. `owner` disposed →
closes. `closeOnNavigate` → closes on navigation. `app.dispose()` and the page's own `pagehide` close every
window and dispose their content; `app.windows.closeAll()` does it on demand.

`onClosing` runs first, before anything is moved: at the window's `pagehide` on a user close, before the host is
disposed otherwise. The window already counts as closed (`isOpen` false, `add` throws `MJX420`) but its document is
still there. `e.components` is a copy of what is in the window; `e.reason` is `'user'` (closed by the user or
`pagehide`), `'code'` (`close()` / `closeAll()`), `'owner'`, `'empty'`, `'navigate'` or `'page'` (the page unloads or
`app.dispose()`). A component the hook gives another parent (`controls.add`) is neither returned nor disposed, its
origin is forgotten and it is missing from `closed`; `win.release` works there too. A throwing hook is reported as
`MJX423` and the close goes on.

## Styles and theme

On open every `<link rel="stylesheet">` and `<style>` of the page (anywhere in the document) is cloned into
the window's head; `adoptedStyleSheets` are rebuilt from their rule text into one `<style>`; `class`, `lang`,
`dir` and `data-*` of `<html>` and `<body>` are mirrored. With `styles: 'live'` (default) later additions,
changes and removals of stylesheets and root attributes follow (two `MutationObserver`s while a live window
is open). Rules added later to an adopted sheet are not observable: call `win.syncStyles()`.

## List and events

`app.windows.list` is reactive (read it in a binding), `app.windows.of(component)` gives the window or
`null`, `app.windows.supports('pip')` tells whether Picture-in-Picture exists. Application events
`window-opened` / `window-closed` carry `{ window }`. A `rel="router"` link inside a window navigates the
page's router; the window is never reloaded.

## Electron

The main process decides on `window.open`; allow the name you pass and give the window its options there:

```ts
win.webContents.setWindowOpenHandler(({ url, frameName }) => {
  if (frameName === 'motif-popup') return { action: 'allow', overrideBrowserWindowOptions: { width: 560, height: 420, alwaysOnTop: true, frame: false } };
  if (/^https?:\/\//.test(url)) void shell.openExternal(url);
  return { action: 'deny' };
});
```

Renderer: `app.windows.open(editor, { name: 'motif-popup' })`. The child shares the opener's renderer process
(also with `file://` pages), so everything above holds. Electron exposes `documentPictureInPicture` but refuses
the request; `fallback` lands on a popup, and `alwaysOnTop` gives the always-on-top window instead. A window
created in the main process with `new BrowserWindow` is another process: no component can move there, talk
over IPC or `MessagePort`.

## Errors

`MJX418` the browser did not open the window (blocker, no gesture) · `MJX419` PiP missing or refused with
`fallback: 'none'` · `MJX420` `add`/`focus` on a closed handle · `MJX421` `attach` got something that is not a
window, or a window of another origin · `MJX422` a disposed component was given to a window · `MJX423` `onClosing`
threw (reported, the close goes on).

---

<!-- references/testing.md -->

# Testing MotifJS components

The framework's own suite uses **Jest + jsdom + ts-jest**, constructing components without JSX so
no compiler step is needed. Mirror that for unit tests; when you need JSX, compile through the
`@motifx/compiler` Vite plugin (Vitest, or Vite + a browser).

## Jest config (jsdom)

```js
// jest.config.cjs
module.exports = {
  testEnvironment: 'jsdom',
  transform: { '^.+\\.tsx?$': ['ts-jest', { tsconfig: { jsx: 'preserve' } }] },
  moduleNameMapper: { '^@motifx/core$': '<rootDir>/node_modules/@motifx/core/dist/index.cjs',
                      '^@motifx/core/devtools$': '<rootDir>/node_modules/@motifx/core/dist/devtools.cjs' },
};
```
In an application, map `@motifx/core` to the installed build `node_modules/@motifx/core/dist/index.cjs`
(and `@motifx/core/devtools` to `dist/devtools.cjs`) exactly as above; no build step is needed.

Working on the framework itself: the monorepo's `packages/tests` mapper points at
`packages/motifjs/dist/index.cjs`, so build `@motifx/core` first (`npm run build --workspace=@motifx/core`,
then `npm test --workspace=motifjs-tests`).

## Pattern

```ts
import { Component, ComponentBase, reactive } from '@motifx/core';
const nextTick = () => Promise.resolve();

test('text binding updates', async () => {
  const data = reactive({ message: 'Hello' });
  const c = new Component('div', {
    initializeComponent: (s: ComponentBase) => { s.bindings.text(() => data.message); },
  });
  c.build();
  document.body.appendChild(c.element as Node);
  await nextTick();
  expect(c.element.textContent).toBe('Hello');

  data.message = 'World';
  await nextTick();
  expect(c.element.textContent).toBe('World');

  await c.dispose();
  expect(c.isDisposed).toBe(true);
});
```

- `component.build()` runs config → initializeComponent → view → built.
- Reactive updates flush on a microtask: `await Promise.resolve()` before asserting.
- Animations: jsdom lacks WAAPI; MotifJS shims it, but await `motif.show()/motif.hide()/dispose()` promises.
- Testing a class with `view()`: instantiate, `build()`, append `element`, assert on
  `element.querySelector(...)`; bindings created by the compiler behave identically to manual ones.
- Events: `element.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }))` after setting `.value`.
- Errors in hooks, event handlers and effects do not throw into the test: they are reported. Capture
  them with `const off = errorHandler.addListener((e) => errors.push(e))` and assert on `e.code`
  (`'MJX122'` hook, `ref` or `x:` listener, `'MJX123'` event handler or `app.on`/`onRouterChanged` listener, `'MJX208'` effect) and `e.cause`; call `off()` afterwards.
- One `Application` per page: call `app.dispose()` at the end of a test before building another
  (it also resets the address to `/` with `history.replaceState`).
- Memory tests: create+dispose inside an inner function, hold a `WeakRef`, call `global.gc()` (run
  Jest with `node --expose-gc`).

## Full-app smoke in jsdom

Load the built Vite bundle via `vite.createServer().ssrLoadModule` or run the real browser with
Playwright; `Application` needs `document` and (for `history` mode) `window.history`.

---

<!-- references/component-libraries.md -->

# Building a component library

A component library (a kit of controls, a data grid, a scheduler) is used by apps it does not know, often with
thousands of its parts on one page. App code can lean on reactivity; library code must not. These rules come from
building a full kit and measuring it. Read `thinking-in-motif.md` and `components.md` first.

## The three ways in

A library component listens to exactly three things:

1. **Its props**, each a value or a function (`Bind<T>`).
2. **The developer's data**, taken as given: kept and handed back as the very objects, never wrapped in `reactive()`,
   copied or converted. A change made in place is read again on `reState()` or on an explicit `refresh()`.
3. **The developer's `reState()`.**

Everything else is the component's own state, and the component draws it by hand.

## Props: a value or a function, followed by one binding

- Every prop and every property setter takes a value or a function. A function is followed by **one** binding of the
  component, registered with `bindings.add(binding)` (the `IBaseBinding` shape, see `jsx-and-reactivity.md`). Being
  in the component's registry is what lets the developer's `reState()` reach it, so plain data works as well as
  reactive data.
- Hand the value on only when it differs from the last one read (`Object.is`). A `reState()` that finds the same
  value must leave what the user did since (a text typed, a day moved to).
- A property set from code stops following its function.
- Render a property with an applier list instead of an effect: apply now and on every change, untracked. No effect
  exists for a property given as a plain value.
- Data objects with function fields (menu items, toolbar items, summary items): read all their fields in **one**
  binding per source, keep the values read and draw from them. Never call the developer's function again while
  drawing: a function that returns a new node makes a new node on every draw.
- A value the user changes too (a text box, a list, a check box) is given to the control only when its source changed,
  not on every draw, or the user's typing is overwritten:

```ts
const handed = new WeakMap<object, { value: unknown }>();
export function handOver<V>(control: { value: V }, value: V) {
  const last = handed.get(control);
  if (last && Object.is(last.value, value)) return;
  handed.set(control, { value });
  control.value = value;
}
```

## Inside, nothing is followed

- **A change is told where it is made.** Each part of the component's state calls `tell(name)`. The names are
  collected and heard once a turn; each view draws again the parts that read what was told. Nothing watches the
  state.
- **What the component does about a change runs before the views.** Loading again, laying out and closing an editor
  run first, and what they tell joins the same turn, so the views draw once. Such a reaction runs when the values it
  reads are no longer the ones it read last. Compare stable values: objects and `Map`s built anew on every read never
  compare equal, so key them as JSON. Put counters in the key too, such as a "read again" version.
- **Tell only on a real change.** A notice told on every draw is a loop: draw, tell, draw. It froze a browser tab.
- **Hand-drawn parts are components made in code.** No JSX there: the compiler makes every expression that reads a
  variable a binding, an attribute too. Also no `bindings.watch` and no free `effect()`. On a data grid page this
  took bindings from 1,306 to 87 and effects run while opening from 2,478 to 346; a sort runs none (was 140).
- **Reactive state may stay for the app.** An API documented as "reactive" (a total, a selected count) can keep its
  store for the app's own bindings; the component never reads it tracked.
- **A language or locale change is an event**, not a signal. Each control subscribes once, draws its texts and
  formats now and again on each change, and the subscription goes with the control:

```ts
export function onLanguage(component: ComponentBase, draw: () => void) {
  untracked(draw);
  const changed = uiLocale.onChanged(() => !component.isDisposed && untracked(draw));
  component.motif.setDisposable(() => changed.dispose());
}
```

- **Static content is built once.** `{cond && <X/>}` and `.map` rows with a `key` cost bindings per item. Content that
  does not change can be built once in `onConfig` or `initializeComponent` with `controls.add`. Done on one docs page,
  this took the page's effects from 16K to 10K.

## The component's tree

- `view()` returns one `ComponentBase`. Several parts go into `motifFragment()`, which is what `<>…</>` compiles to.
- Parts that must be direct children of the element (header cells, rows that are moved) are added in
  `initializeComponent` (an override), not returned from `view()`.
- Keyed parts are reconciled by hand. Never move a node that is already in its place: moving the focused element
  takes its focus.
- `controls.remove(part)` takes the part out at once. `part.dispose()` removes its element a turn later, so a draw
  right after it still finds the element.
- A part shown and hidden in its place, like `x-display`, is swapped for a comment placeholder and put back there. A
  placeholder needs a parent, so draw top-level parts the first time in `onBuilt`.

## Writes are change-checked

- Writing an attribute, a style or a text again with the same value still makes the browser work the styles out
  again. Hand-drawn code that rewrote unchanged attributes on every draw had five times the style recalculation of
  the reactive code it replaced. Write a value only when it changed.
- Replacing a constructable stylesheet (`replaceSync`) with the same text invalidates the styles of the whole
  document. A grid that rewrote its per-column sheet on every step of a column resize spent 60–110 ms per step; writing
  the sheet only when its text changed removed the long tasks.

## Lifetime

- Disposing a component clears its own fields to `undefined`. Callbacks that come later (timers, promises,
  observers, a deferred draw) check `isDisposed` first.
- `onDisposing` runs before the element leaves the DOM, and removing a focused element fires `focusout`. A
  `focusout` handler can therefore run on a component that is being disposed.
- When focus has to move off a control that is hidden or disabled, focus the next one with
  `focus({ preventScroll: true })`, or the page scrolls to it.
- `ref` callbacks run inside the base constructor, before the subclass's field initializers. State that a `ref` may
  touch lives on a lazily created, symbol-keyed object, not in class fields.

## Long work

- `Promise.then` and `queueMicrotask` do not let the browser paint: a chain of microtasks is still one long task.
  Split long work with macrotasks (`setTimeout`, `MessageChannel`). Measured: one 300 ms long task as microtasks, no
  long task and 18 painted frames as `setTimeout` pieces.

## Checking the work

- Count bindings per component type by walking the component tree (`devtools` `inspect(path).bindings`), not only
  live effects: a binding that follows a prop has no effect owner and is missing from an effect count.
- Rewrite a view under a pixel comparison of old and new on every page of it. Keep its tests and e2e checks green at
  every step, and prove the effect count went down.
- An e2e check that reads the page right after `load` waits for the content first: pages draw their sections after
  `load`.

---

<!-- references/api-cheatsheet.md -->

# API cheat-sheet (`import { ... } from '@motifx/core'`)

Ground truth: `node_modules/@motifx/core/dist/index.d.ts` (value + type exports), `dist/jsx-runtime.d.ts`
(JSX types) and `dist/devtools.d.ts` (`@motifx/core/devtools` subpath).

## Application

```ts
Application.CreateBuilder(): ApplicationBuilder      // .services: ServiceCollection; .build(): Application; .rebuild()
Application.main: Application                        // global instance
app.run(host: string | HTMLElement | Node, root?: ComponentBase): void   // no root → default <RouterView name="default"/>; a comment or text node host: the app goes right before it and the node stays (MJX416 when it has no parent element); a disposed app runs again with run(): Application.main refilled, services created anew on demand, a fresh router from the config, the useTransitions mode re-applied, a layer read in between moved after the host, dispose() works again (MJX405 when a newer app was built meanwhile)
app.useRouter(routes | { routes, mode?, fallbacks?, hooks?, scrollMemory?, stack? }): Application
app.useGuard((ctx: { to, from }, next: (to?: string | false) => void) => void): Application
app.use((ctx: RouteResolveContext, next) => any): Application        // ctx: { uri, context, rewritePath(uri) }
app.navigate(uri, options?: NavigationOptions): Promise<any>         // options are forwarded to the router; resolves to the navigation result, e.g. { ok: false, cancelled: true, reason: 'guard' }
app.navigateByName(name, params?, options?: NavigationOptions): Promise<any>
app.router.navigate(uri, options?: NavigationOptions): Promise<any>  // { replace?, state?, force?, scroll? }
app.router.params / .route / .uri / .ok / .meta / .extend / .chain   // one object per app; read-only, reactive
app.router.direction   // 'initial' | 'push' | 'replace' | 'back' | 'forward' | 'traverse'
app.router.state       // the `state` given to navigate() for the current history entry; comes back on back/forward and reload
app.router.stack       // only with useRouter({ stack }): [{ index, uri, current, retained }]
app.router.fullPath / app.router.aliasOf             // matched pattern / canonical pattern when matched via alias (else null)
app.router.evict(nameOrRoute?): Promise<void>      // release cached keepAlive instances (no argument → all); unknown name rejects with MJX302
app.router.resolve(uri): RouteResolution              // match without navigating: { chain: string[] (like router.chain), result: ResolveResult (what navigate returns; result.chain: RouteItem[]) }
app.router.href(name, params?): string               // path of a named route (throws MJX302 for an unknown name)
app.router.routes: RouteInfo[]                        // route table in definition order: { fullPath, name, meta, route, chain }
app.router.scrollPositions(): Record<string, number>   // scroll memory positions { '/notes': 1200 }, shown page included; {} while scrollMemory is off
app.router.restoreScrollPositions(positions): void    // add saved positions back (limit applies; callable before run()); no-op while off
app.router.saveScrollPositions(fn): () => void        // fn(positions) whenever saving is due (leaving a page, pagehide, hidden, app.dispose()); survives restartRouter; returns unsubscribe
app.on(event, handler) → unsubscribe fn; app.off(event, handler); app.fire(event, args?)
app.onRouterChanged((e: RouterNavigatedEventArgs) => …) → unsubscribe fn   // { uri, params, meta, route, ok, initial, redirectedFrom?, direction, state }; every navigation incl. initial + 404
app.onLifecycle(({ state, visible, online }) => …) → unsubscribe fn   // state: 'visible'|'hidden'|'frozen'|'resumed'|'restored'|'online'|'offline'; listeners installed lazily, removed by app.dispose(); never tied to a component, also not through this.context: call the unsubscribe yourself
app.isVisible; app.isOnline
app.useDevelopment(bool = true); app.useLogging(bool = true); app.useReactiveMonitor({ enabled, threshold, name, dependencies, scans })
app.isDevelopmentModeEnabled; app.restartRouter(uri?): Promise<result> (builds a fresh router from the latest useRouter config and starts it at '/' or at uri, replacing the history entry: routes, keepAlive cache and stack reset, scroll memory kept; the shown page leaves like a leaving page, a given/singleton layout at the same place stays; guards run, a cancel leaves the screen empty; onRouterChanged fires with initial: true; resolves to the startup navigation's result, undefined before run)
app.connectDocument(doc: Document): () => void   // same-origin popup/iframe document: router links and stack swipes listen there too; counted, released by the returned fn or the window's pagehide; the page's own document is a no-op; MJX417 for a value that is not a usable document
app.windows: WindowManager   // open(component, options?): Promise<AppWindow> (= create + add; call inside a user gesture) · create(options?) · attach(window, options?) · of(component): AppWindow | null · supports('popup' | 'pip') · closeAll() · list (reactive) · events 'window-opened' / 'window-closed' { window }
  // options: kind 'popup' | 'pip', fallback 'popup' | 'none', width, height, left, top, name (Electron frameName), features, title, styles 'live' | 'once' | 'none' | (doc) => void, orphans 'dispose' | 'keep', closeWhenEmpty, closeOnNavigate, returnOnClose (false: content with an origin follows orphans too), owner, onClosing(e: { window, components, reason: 'user' | 'code' | 'owner' | 'empty' | 'navigate' | 'page' }) — before teardown, content still in the window; what it moves to another parent is neither returned nor disposed
  // AppWindow: window, document, host, kind ('popup' | 'pip' | 'attached'), components, isOpen, add(...c), release(c), focus(), close(): Promise<{ returned, disposed, kept }>, closed, syncStyles(); MJX418 not opened, MJX419 pip missing/refused, MJX420 closed handle, MJX421 not a window or another origin, MJX422 disposed component, MJX423 onClosing threw (reported)
app.layer: Component   // page layer: a plain <div> at the end of <body>, after the run() host (when the host is <body> itself or contains the layer, the layer stays last and the shell's content is inserted before it), created on first read; no styles/attributes from the core (add class/attr yourself); readable before run() (joins at DOMContentLoaded while body is missing, content mounts then; an element taken out of the page comes back at the end of body with its content when content next needs a place or at run()); a root like the shell (parent null); app.dispose() disposes it with its content and removes the element
app.layerOf(target?, ...components): Component   // layer of the document holding target (component or DOM node): a window's host when it lives in a window from app.windows, else app.layer; no/null target → app.layer; the components are controls.add-ed there and the layer is returned; a first component with no parent and an element in no document counts as content, a parentless root already in a document (new Component(document.body)) is a target (this.context.layerOf(this, toast) → the component's window or the page, this.context.layerOf(toast) → the page); MJX424 when target is neither a component nor a node
app.provider: ServiceProvider; app.getAppShell(): Component; app.dispose(): Promise<void>   // sync: state 'disposing', router, lifecycle listeners, address reset by mode (history '/', hash/file clears '#', shell/no router untouched); then pages (leave animations), RouterView, run() shell, LAST the provider (async disposes awaited) and Application.main = null; components keep seeing services/context until then; a second call in the same life returns the same promise; after run() again dispose() runs again; on a disposed app dispose() releases what was created since (layer, windows, documents, services) without touching the address, and a call while that pass runs joins it; the host element stays
app.state: 'initializing' | 'running' | 'disposing' | 'disposed'   // a new CreateBuilder() is allowed while the previous app is 'disposing'; its torn-down pages still resolve their own app
app.insert(c) / app.attach(c)  // add to the app shell; app.remove(c) (dispose) / app.detach(c) (no dispose); app.appendToMainHost(node)
useNavigation(): Router   // the same object as app.router; read nav.params.id live, destructuring keeps that moment's value
useApplication(): { application, services, router, windows, layer, layerOf, attach(...components) }   // application = Application.main
```

Inside a component `this.context` is the application seen through a component-scoped view:
`this.context.on(...)` and `this.context.onRouterChanged(...)` subscriptions are removed
automatically when the component is disposed; `this.context.onLifecycle(...)` is not (keep its
unsubscribe and pass it to `this.motif.setDisposable`). Calling `on` on `Application.main`, a captured
`app` or `useApplication().application` is not tied to any component.

## Components

```ts
class Component<TElement = any, TProps extends object = any> extends ComponentBase<TElement, TProps>
  static elementTag?: string; static elementNamespace?: string
  constructor(elementOrProps?: TElement | string | IBaseProp<TProps>, props?: IBaseProp<TProps>)
FNComponent(view: (props) => JSX): (props) => FragmentNode
FragmentNode, Frame, Transport, TransportTo, ContentBody, ContentBlock, RouterView, RouterLink, Virtualization<T>
Lazy({ caller: () => Promise<T>, options?: LazyOptions<T> }): Component      // a function, used as <Lazy …/>
motifComponent(el, props?), motifFragment(props?), motifCompiled(contract), motifReport(error)   // what the compiler emits (_mc / _mf / _mv / _mr); MJX121 on a contract mismatch (dev); motifReport reports a caught getter error as MJX208
motifOptions(spec)                       // Options object as is; types `this` in its methods as ComponentBase & spec (MotifOptions<T>)

// ComponentBase members
element, props, childs, parent, context, controls, bindings, class, attr, motif
view?(): any; initializeComponent?(sender): void; oninitializeComponent?(sender, e): void
onInitializing/onInitialized/onConfig/onConfigured/onBuilding/onBuilt/onMounted/onVisibilityChanged/onActivated/onDeactivated/onDisposing/onDisposed(sender, e)
onRefCreated?(sender)   // after each ref={this.x} / ref={name} in this class's view(); not for callback refs
build(); setState(); reState(); setText(s); style(v)
isVisible; isWait (get/set)
dispose(opts?: { deep?, skipLeaveTransition? }): Promise<void>; disposeAsync(opts?)
using(promise, onfulfilled?, onrejected?)   // returns nothing; callbacks skipped once disposed; value typed from the promise; a callback that throws (or rejects) is reported as MJX129; a rejection with no onrejected is dropped
doWork(promise): Promise<T | MotifError>    // value while alive, a rejection passes on; once disposed resolves to MotifError MJX108 (never rejects), a rejection becomes its cause
getService(token): T | null  // T from any class token (constructor params, abstract, protected ctor); getService<T>(Class) gives the same T; getService<T>(stringOrSymbol) otherwise. Same rule for FromService, inject, provider.get/getAsync. serviceProvider; useModel(obj)
$(selector): { fromDom(), fromComponent() }; siblings.{all,next,prev,nextAll,prevAll}()
isBuilt, isInitialized (false in onInitializing, true from onInitialized on), isConfigured, isDisposed

// component.motif (ComponentMotif): framework operations; a subclass may define its own show/on/clear/options
motif.on(event, cb, domEvent = true): Promise<this>; motif.off(event, cb): Promise<this>; motif.trigger(event, args): Promise<this>; motif.addHandler(event, handler)
motif.show(): Promise; motif.hide(): Promise; motif.toggle()
motif.clear(): Promise; motif.register(d: IDisposable); motif.setDisposable(fn); motif.stopAnimations(): Promise<void>
motif.options                                          // transition, hideStrategy, disableDisposal, chunk
```

`Frame`: `navigate(component | component[], keepOldControl = false)`, `navigateLazy(caller, options?, keepOldControl?)`,
`flush()`, `current`, `isBusy`, `motif.clear()`.

`Transport` props `{ name, mode?: 'replace' | 'merge' }` (+ `clearSlot()`); `TransportTo` props `{ name }`.
`ContentBody` props `{ name }`; `ContentBlock` props `{ target }`.
`Transporter.transport(child, newParent, options?)`, `transportMany(children, newParent, options?)`,
`createSlot(name, parent?)` — the low-level mover behind `Transport` (`TransportOptions { index?, keepState?, owner? }`).
`transport` unlinks the child from its old parent and adds it to the new one; the child stays alive (not disposed).
With `index` the child is placed at that position in the new parent's element; `transportMany` places the children in the given order from that index.

## ControlCollection (`component.controls`)

`add(...c)` / `add(index, ...c)`, `insert(index, ...c)`, `remove(c)` (dispose), `clear()` / `clearAsync()` (dispose all),
`detach(c): Promise<void>` (leave animation, no dispose), `silentDetach(c)`, `silentUnlink(c)`,
`move(c, before?)`, `moveToIndex(c, index)`, `forEach(fn)`, `map(fn)`, `items`, `length`, `onAdd`, `onRemove`.

## BindingCollection (`component.bindings`)

`add`, `text`, `value`, `html`, `when`, `ternary`, `list`, `loop`, `switchCase`, `method`, `watch`, `model`, `wait`, `display`, `remove`, `clear`, `items`. See jsx-and-reactivity.md.

## Reactivity

```ts
reactive<T>(m: T): T; useModel<T>(m: T): T   // a number, string or boolean is boxed: reactive('') is { value: '' }
createSignal<T>(v): Signal<T>; new Signal(v, equals?); Signal.create(v, equals?); createComputed<T>(fn): Computed<T>; createLazyComputed<T>(fn): LazyComputed<T>
createSelection<T>(fn): KeySelection<T>   // isSelected(key) subscribes to that key only; a source change wakes only the previous and the new key; .dispose()
asReadonly<T>(o): DeepReadonly<T>; isReadonly(v): boolean   // live read-only view (no copy); writes, deletes, mutating array methods and Map/Set changes throw MJX212
effect(fn, onValueChanged?): () => void   // onValueChanged(value) runs after every run of fn (the first included) with fn's return value, untracked; a run in which fn throws has no value: onValueChanged is not called, MJX208 is reported, tracking continues
untracked(fn): T; deepClone(v); clearModel(m)
Signal: value, peek(), update(fn), mutate(fn), notify(), asReadonly(): ReadonlySignal<T>, dispose()
Computed: value, peek(), dispose(); LazyComputed: value, peek(), isDirty, dispose()
type Bind<T> = T | (() => T); toGetter(v: Bind<T>): () => T; read(v: Bind<T>): T
configureReactivityLeakMonitor({ enabled?, threshold?, name?, dependencies? })   // same switch as app.useReactiveMonitor; dependencies = per-run dependency limit of one effect (1000, MJX209; 0 off); scans = runtime list-scan warning MJX210 (default on, false off)
asyncTracking                                                    // emitted around the awaits of an async function written inline on <Virtualization dataRequest>; not for app code
```

`import { debugGetDeps, debugGetDepMap } from '@motifx/core/devtools'` — dependency maps of reactive objects (tests/diagnostics).

Devtools: `app.useDevelopment(true)` is the only switch. It turns on development mode (dev warnings, the route
linter) and devtools together; `useDevelopment(false)` turns both off. A URL parameter or a global set by hand never
turns devtools on. While devtools are on, `globalThis.__MOTIF_DEVTOOLS__` holds the contract object, typed
`MotifDevtools` from `@motifx/core/devtools` (`version: 2`). An external devtools panel
connects through it. Components have no ids: the tree is a forest. `[]` is a virtual `Application` node, `path[0]`
picks a root (0 the `run()` shell, then `app.layer` as `Layer` once it exists, then the `host` of every `app.windows`
window as `Window`, in `app.windows.list` order) and the rest are `controls` indexes down from that root; a component
under no root has path `null`. Paths shift when lists change and when a root comes or goes, which `tree:changed`
reports (`[]` for the root list).

```ts
on(fn) => off                         // fn({ type, payload })
getTree(path = [], depth = Infinity)  // { path, type, tag, built, visible, waiting, disposed, connected, document, childCount, children? }; type = class name or function name
                                      // [] is { type: 'Application', tag: '#roots' }; a window root carries title; document = index into getDocuments() (0 = the page), kept for a component whose element the app moved to another document
                                      // a .map() list shows as List (its place) > ListItems (the item range) > items
                                      // conditions show as Ternary / When / Expression / Switch holding the content, or Empty; x-wait adds nothing
coreVersion                           // version of @motifx/core, next to version (the contract version, 2)
getElement(path) / pathOfElement(node) // in any document of the app; null for [] and for a node under no root
getDocuments()                        // the page document first, then the connected ones (app.windows windows, connectDocument); documents:changed says when to reread
inspect(path)                         // props (getters not called), fields (own fields, framework internals left out), functionProps (function component root), bindings, events, hooks, classes, attributes, services, effects, extensions, window (window roots only: { kind, title, open, components })
readValue(path, 'props' | 'functionProps' | 'fields', keys) // one level of a nested value: { value, entries: [{ key, value, getter? }], total }
                                      // a signal or computed previews as { kind: 'signal', type, value, stale? }; paths continue into its value
readStore(id, keys)                   // same, for a store from getStores()
readService(scope, token, keys)       // same, for a service instance listed by getScopes(); never creates a service
getCounters()                         // components { live, inTree, notInTree, byType }, bindings, listeners, effects, reactivity
getWarnings() / getErrors()           // grouped by code+message / context+name+message, with count, firstAt, lastAt
getRoute() / getNavigations() / getRoutes() / getServices()
getScopes()                           // DI scopes: { id, kind: 'root' | 'navigation' | 'user', name, parent, current, pending, pins, services: [{ token, lifetime, instance, creating? }], transients }
                                      // pins: components outside the current page still keeping the scope (keepAlive)
getStores()                           // stores still in use: { id, name, file?, type: 'reactive' | 'signal' | 'computed', value, stale?, released?, holders }
                                      // top-level module stores are named by the compiler while developing (name = variable, file = path);
                                      // early stores kept in a component or service field are found by the scan; stores kept only in a closure are not
                                      // holders: components/services keeping it in a field, e.g. { kind: 'component', path, type, field }
getExtensions() / readExtension(name)
readExtensionPanels(name)             // { panels, sources: { [name]: { key?, events?, max? } }, commands: string[] }; a panel's shape beyond id and capabilities is the devtools panel's own schema
readExtensionSource(name, panel, source, params)   // awaits the source's read(params); needs read on that panel → { ok: true, value } | { ok: false, error }
callExtension(name, panel, command, args)          // runs a package command; needs write on that panel; the awaited return value is value
setClass(path, name, on) / setAttribute(path, name, value | null) / setVisible(path, visible)   // setVisible on a root → { ok: false }
writeModel(path, value) / setProp(path, keys, value) / navigate(uri) / setStoreValue(id, keys, value)
                                      // writes go through public APIs; result { ok, value? } | { ok: false, error }
```

Events: `tree:changed` (`parents`; `[]` when the root list changed), `documents:changed` (reread `getDocuments()`), `component:built`, `component:visibility`, `component:wait`, `component:disposing`,
`component:disposed` (payloads carry `{ path, type, tag }`; `path` is `null` under no root), `reactivity:flush` (once per reactivity turn: `{ id, duration, runs, triggers, effects, operations }`; a trigger names its store as `store: { id, path }` and the operation it ran in as `operationId`), `stores:changed` (new stores recorded, once per turn), `scopes:changed` (a DI scope opened, committed or disposed, once per turn),
`service:created` (`{ scope, token, lifetime, source: 'class' | 'factory' | 'value', instance }`; transients on every resolution), `service:disposed` (`{ scope, token, lifetime, instance }`),
`route:navigation-start`, `route:navigation-end` (`outcome`: `done`, `skipped`, `cancelled`, `notFound`, `error`),
`operation:started` (`{ id, kind, name?, data?, parent? }`), `operation:finished` (`{ id, duration, error? }`),
`extension:registered` / `extension:disposed` (`{ name }`), `extension:changed` (`{ name, source? }`), `extension:reveal` (`{ name, target }`),
`warning`, `error:caught`, `ext:<name>:<type>`. There is no mounted event; read `connected` from the tree.

`notInTree` counts living components that are not in the tree; when it does not drop after leaving a page, those
components are still held somewhere.

A package exposes its own state with
`registerDevtools(name, { describe?, inspect?(component), sources?, commands?, panels? })` from `@motifx/core/devtools`;
it returns `{ emit(type, payload), pathOf(component), changed(source?), reveal(target), dispose() }`. Registration is
free while devtools are off; `describe`, `inspect`, `sources`, `commands` and a `panels` function run only when the
panel asks. `panels` are `{ id, title, icon?, order?, capabilities?: { read?, subscribe?, write? }, … }`: the core
reads only `id` and `capabilities` (checked per panel on every `readExtensionSource` / `callExtension`; `emit` is
silent while a registration with panels has none subscribing), the rest is the devtools panel's own schema. `sources`
are `{ read(params), key?, events?, max? }`, `commands` plain functions, both looked up by own key only; a throw
answers `{ ok: false, error }`. `changed(source?)` and `reveal({ panel, route?, params?, state? })` publish
`extension:changed` / `extension:reveal` while the registration is the current one under its name.

Operations and write records, for packages that keep a history or draw a timeline (not for app code):
`runOperation(info, fn)`, `startOperation(info) => { id, kind, name?, data?, parent? }`,
`resumeOperation(operation | null, fn)`, `endOperation(operation, error?)`, `currentOperation()`. An operation is
"the work running now", one value like the running effect — not a context, nothing is passed down; `parent` is the
operation running when this one started. `runOperation` with a promise-returning `fn` ends when it settles and
returns a promise that follows it (same value, same rejection); with devtools off it returns `fn`'s result as it is.
Nothing survives an `await`: resume by hand, never rely on `currentOperation()` after `await`. Writes, flush triggers
(`operationId`) and `operation:started` / `operation:finished` carry the id; resuming an ended operation warns once
(`MJX211`). `onWrite(fn) => off` reports every reactive write while devtools are on:
`{ target, operationId?, kind: 'add' | 'update' | 'delete' | 'clear' | 'splice' | 'mutate', … }` with `key` /
`previous` / `value`, `clear.removed`, `splice` as `{ method, index, removed, added }` (one per array method,
`method: 'length'` for a shortened length), `mutate` for `signal.mutate`. Values are references; no-op writes and a
listener's own writes are not reported; every report is `@DEV-ONLY`, dropped from production builds — a tool for
package authors, not an undo primitive.

## DI

```ts
ServiceCollection: addSingleton/addScoped/addTransient(token, impl), tryAdd*(token, impl): boolean, replace(token, impl, lifetime?), remove(token), has(token), reset(), getDescriptor(token), buildServiceProvider()
ServiceProvider: get(token), getAsync(token), createScope(name?), dispose()
Injectable({ lifetime?, deps?, startup? }), inject(token) → instance (only during provider construction, else MJX409), FromService(token) → instance | null (dev warning MJX414 on failure); all three type the result from a class token, `<T>` only for string/symbol tokens; add*(token, fn) with a non-constructible fn → MJX413
type ServiceLifetime = 'transient' | 'singleton' | 'scoped'
startup: true   // on @Injectable or the add* object form ({ useClass | useFactory, startup: true }): a singleton created inside app.run() and again on builder.rebuild()
```

## Routing

```ts
type RouteItem = { path, control?, childs?, name?, meta?, extend?, keepAlive?, redirect?: string | ((to: { path, params, meta }) => string), alias?: string | string[], validate?, onShow?, onEntering?, onEnter?, onLeave?, onUpdate? }   // control or redirect required
RouterView({ name? }); RouterLink({ to, el?: string | Node, activeClass?, exactClass?, onActive?, offActive?, onExact?, offExact?, showHref?, target?, text?, bypass? })   // renders <a> unless el is given; showHref:false omits href; bypass, a target other than '_self' and Ctrl/Cmd/Shift/Alt clicks are left to the browser; text = link text when there are no children
types: RouterOptions, ScrollMemoryOptions, NavigationOptions, NavigationGuard, NavigationGuardContext, RouterNavigatedEventArgs, RouteRedirect, RedirectTarget, RouterEvents, ResolveResult, RouteInfo
```

## Disposal

`IDisposable { dispose() }`, `Disposable`, `DisposableStore { add, delete, clear, dispose, isDisposed }`,
`disposableCore.toDisposable(fn)` / `toDisposable(fn)`, `disposableCore.disposableTracker` (live-instance
counting, see lifecycle-and-dispose.md).

## Collections and queries

`Query.from(iterable)` / `new Query(iterable)`: `where`, `select`, `orderBy`, `orderByDescending`, `distinctBy`,
`groupBy` (→ `Query<Group<TKey, T>>`, `Group { key, items }`) chain; `toArray`, `first`, `firstOrDefault`,
`any(pred?)`, `all(pred)`, `aggregate(seed, fn)` finish; a `Query` is iterable. Eager (each step builds an
array); the source is never mutated. Arrays have no LINQ methods of their own.
`List`, `Dictionary`, `LinkedList`, `NameValuePair`.

## Errors, utilities

`MotifError` (`Error` subclass with `code: MotifErrorCode`, an `MJX…` code; the framework throws it and passes it to `errorHandler` listeners; `MJX503` carries the individual dispose errors in `cause.errors`),
`errorHandler` (`ErrorHandler`: `addListener(fn) → unbind`, listeners called in order; one that throws does not stop the others or the reporting code, its error is rethrown in a `setTimeout`, so `safeCall` still returns its fallback; `setUnexpectedErrorHandler`, `safeCall`…),
`setUnexpectedErrorHandler(fn)` (receives uncoded errors caught by `safeCall`/`safeCallAsync` and by `Emitter` listeners, which also reach `addListener` as they are; the default rethrows in a `setTimeout`; coded reports such as `MJX122`/`MJX123`/`MJX208` never reach it),
`safeCall(fn, context, fallback?)`, `safeCallAsync`, `safeCallSilent`,
`Resilience.create.retry({...}).timeout({ timeoutMs }).circuitBreaker(...).bulkhead(...).rateLimiter(...).fallback({ fallback }).execute(fn)`
(`rateLimiter` defaults: `tokensPerInterval` 1, `intervalMs` 1000, `capacity` = `tokensPerInterval`),
`decorate(policy, fn)`, `dom.createElement/createElementNS/createComment/createTextNode`,
`NodeTypes`, `Emitter<T>` / `Event`, `preProcessing`.
Types: `EventArgs { cancel }`, `TransitionProps`, `IBaseProp<T>`, `LazyOptions`, `Virtualization*` types,
resilience types `RetryOptions`, `TimeoutOptions`, `CircuitBreakerOptions`, `CircuitState`, `BulkheadOptions`,
`RateLimiterOptions`, `FallbackOptions<T>`, `ResiliencePolicy` (what `decorate` accepts; `Resilience` implements it),
`ResilienceAction<T>`, `ResilienceContext`.

`Emitter<T>`: `fire(value)`, `event` (an `Event<T>`: `(listener, thisArgs?, disposables?) => IDisposable`),
`dispose()`. A service exposing an event:

```ts
class CartService {
  private readonly changed = new Emitter<Item[]>();
  readonly onChanged: Event<Item[]> = this.changed.event;
  add(item: Item) { this.items.push(item); this.changed.fire(this.items); }
}
this.motif.register(cart.onChanged(items => …));   // the IDisposable is released with the component
```

## MJX codes

`MotifError.code`; messages read `[motifjs] MJX…: …`. "Thrown" errors reach the caller; "reported" ones go
to `errorHandler.addListener` (original error in `cause`); "dev warning" prints only in development.

| Code | Kind | When |
|---|---|---|
| `MJX101` | thrown | creating an element with no `document` (SSR / plain Node) |
| `MJX108` | value | `doWork(p)` resolves to this `MotifError` (does not reject) when the component was disposed meanwhile; if `p` rejected, the rejection is its `cause` |
| `MJX110` / `MJX111` | `Lazy` load error | `timeoutMs` elapsed / `signal` aborted; passed to `onError` (after a timeout `Fallbackview` is shown) |
| `MJX126` | reported | a `Lazy` load failed with no `Fallbackview`; the host was cleared, original error in `cause` |
| `MJX127` | thrown | a lazy route or `Lazy` loaded a module with no `default` export (or another non-component object; null/text/arrays/promises are placed as before); router: `cause` of `MJX304` + error route; `Lazy`: load failure. Fix: `export default`, or `() => import('./X').then(m => m.X)` |
| `MJX128` | dev warning | a class component hides a `ComponentBase` member: override without `super` (`build`, `dispose`, `style` …), an instance field over a method/accessor, or a replaced `controls`/`attr`/`class`/`bindings`/`motif`/`element`/`parent`; once per class, behavior unchanged |
| `MJX129` | reported | an `onfulfilled`/`onrejected` callback given to `using` threw or returned a rejected promise; original error in `cause` |
| `MJX130` | reported | a child sliced by `x-chunk` threw while being built on its turn; the other children of the slice still build; a `.map` row that threw keeps its trace and is created again on the list's next update; original error in `cause` |
| `MJX121` | dev warning | compiled code's compiler contract differs from the `@motifx/core` runtime |
| `MJX122` | reported | a component hook, `ref` callback or `x:` lifecycle listener threw (`The component onBuilt hook threw.`) |
| `MJX123` | reported | an event handler or application event listener threw (`The 'click' event handler threw.`) |
| `MJX124` | dev warning | a spread object on a DOM tag carried `innerHTML` or `srcdoc`; the key was ignored |
| `MJX125` | dev warning | a spread object on a DOM tag carried a `javascript:` URL for `href`/`src`/`action`/`formaction`/`xlink:href`; the value was ignored |
| `MJX201` | thrown | a list `renderFn` returned something that is not a component, class or factory |
| `MJX202` | dev warning | duplicate list `key` (rendering unaffected) |
| `MJX203` | dev warning | an effect ran 50 times in one flush; skipped for the rest of that flush |
| `MJX209` | dev warning | an effect tracked more than `dependencies` (1000) values in one run, once per effect, at most ten times; names the owner component and binding when devtools are on; look items up by key or read the list with `untracked` |
| `MJX210` | dev warning | two or more instances of one component (eight owner-less effects) scan the same reactive list with `find`/`findIndex`/`findLast`/`findLastIndex`/`some`/`every` and the list has at least as many items as there are scanners, wherever it came from (props, another module, a service); instances are component objects, a three-item settings list read by a hundred rows stays quiet; once per list, at most ten times, needs devtools on; keep a keyed `Map` or a computed index, or read the list with `untracked`; `useReactiveMonitor({ scans: false })` switches it off |
| `MJX211` | dev warning | `resumeOperation` on an operation that already ended; its writes are still recorded under it. End after the last write, or use `startOperation` / `endOperation` for work that spans callbacks |
| `MJX212` | thrown | a write, delete, mutating array method or `Map`/`Set` change through an `asReadonly` view; nothing changes. Change the data through the reactive object the view was made from |
| `MJX204` | dev warning | a component reached a text binding (template prop assigned after setup; write `{() => props.tpl}`) |
| `MJX205` | reported | `Virtualization` `watch` callback threw |
| `MJX206` | dev warning | `Virtualization` `autoRefresh` stopped (`dataRequest` keeps changing the data it reads) |
| `MJX207` | reported | `Virtualization` data load failed |
| `MJX208` | reported | an effect threw; that run has no value, `onValueChanged` is not called |
| `MJX301` | dev warning | a layout's `RouterView` outlet was not built within 3000 ms |
| `MJX302` | thrown | `href` / `evict` with an unknown route name |
| `MJX303` | dev warning | redirect loop or more than 10 redirects; `fallbacks.error` renders |
| `MJX304` / `MJX305` | reported | a route control failed to construct or load / the error fallback itself failed |
| `MJX306` | reported | a route hook, `onShow` or guard threw (a guard cancels the navigation) |
| `MJX309` | thrown | navigating before `useRouter()` |
| `MJX310`–`MJX316` | dev warning | route linter: empty path, child path/alias without `/`, child equals parent path, duplicate full path, alias equals own path, duplicate alias |
| `MJX319` | dev warning | route linter: `:` outside braces in a path or alias (`/user/:id`); parameters are `{name}`, `:` only gives a default inside braces |
| `MJX320` | dev warning | route linter: a parameter pattern cannot be used (does not compile, `(` never closed, or `/` inside; a pattern applies to one segment) |
| `MJX321` | dev warning | `mode: 'history'` on a `file:` address; the router runs in hash mode |
| `MJX401` | thrown | token not registered (and not `@Injectable`) |
| `MJX404` | thrown | cyclic service dependency |
| `MJX405` | thrown | second `Application.CreateBuilder()` while an app is running (allowed once the previous app is `'disposing'`) |
| `MJX406` | thrown | `app.run(selector)` found no host |
| `MJX409` | thrown | `inject()` outside a provider construction |
| `MJX413` | thrown | `add*(token, fn)` with a non-constructible function |
| `MJX414` | dev warning | `FromService` failed; it returns `null` |
| `MJX415` | dev warning | `startup` on a `transient` or `scoped` registration; it is ignored |
| `MJX416` | thrown | `app.run(node)` got a comment or text node that has no parent element |
| `MJX503` | thrown | several disposables threw while disposing a store (errors in `cause.errors`) |
| `MJX507` | dev warning | leak monitor (`app.useReactiveMonitor` / `configureReactivityLeakMonitor`): the effects tracking one field reached `threshold` |
| `MJX601` | thrown | `Query.first()` on an empty sequence |
| `MJX602`–`MJX605` | thrown | `Resilience`: circuit open / bulkhead queue full / rate limit exceeded / timeout (`TimeoutError`) |

Compiler (`@motifx/compiler`): warnings `MJX001` (block-bodied arrow with parameters in child position declares locals the
branches cannot see), `MJX002` (camelCase DOM event name on a component tag), `MJX003` (`.map()` item without
`key`), `MJX004` (a reactive getter scans a reactive list by key: `find`/`findIndex`/`some`/`every` with an `x.field === value`
predicate; n components doing this cost n² reads per change, keep a keyed map or read with `untracked`), `MJX017` (a reactive
getter writes a reactive value it also reads: `++`, `+=` or an assignment to a field read elsewhere in the getter; it retriggers
itself; plain class fields and fields the getter never reads are fine; to keep a latch, read the flag inside `untracked`, wrapping
the write alone does not help), `MJX018` (`sort`/`reverse` on a reactive list inside a
reactive getter, or `push`/`pop`/`shift`/`unshift`/`splice` when the getter also reads that list; work on a copy; these three
checks recognise `this.state`, `this.props`, class fields built with a core store factory in an initializer or the constructor,
same-file module stores and aliases of those inside the getter, and count callbacks of synchronous array methods as part of
the getter; imported stores, stores created inside a function, injected services and a function component's `props` are not recognised), `MJX007` (unknown `x-*` directive, passed on
as `on<name>`), `MJX015` (a class component override of a `ComponentBase` method/accessor that does not reach
`super` on every path; also checked in `.ts`/`.js` files, base followed across files), `MJX016` (a `switch` or
`return a ? b : c` getter that cannot be lowered runs as `bindings.method`, no branch is kept); `MJX005` from `motif-lint`
(ternary on a prop not typed `Bind<T>`), which also reports `MJX015`; build errors `MJX006`
(unsupported directive), `MJX008` (`function () {}` as a JSX child), `MJX009` (string/boolean event handler),
`MJX010` (invalid lifecycle hook value), `MJX011` / `MJX012` (invalid directive value / object literal, or an `x-chunk` value that cannot be a number),
`MJX013` (namespaced tag name such as `<svg:rect>`, or a spread child `{...items}`; a lowercase non-HTML
name such as `<card>` is no error, it resolves to the identifier in scope and a missing one fails at runtime
with `ReferenceError`); `MJX014` (`motif-lint` cannot read the tsconfig).

## JSX-only props

`key`, `ref` / `x-ref`, `x-html`, `x-wait`, `x-display`, `x-chunk`, `x-style`, `initializeComponent` (plain and component tags),
`transition`, `childs`, `on<event>[:modifier]` (one modifier per attribute), `on:name` / `on-name` / `on_name`
(handler passed as is to `motif.on(name, fn)`), `on<lifecycle>` / `x-<lifecycle>` / `x:<lifecycle>`
(`onMounted`, `onActivated`, `onDeactivated`… included; several spellings on one tag all run in source order), `options={{ hideStrategy, disableDisposal }}`,
method-like props that call the element method and write no attribute (`focus`, `blur`, `click`, `select`, `scrollIntoView`, `show`/`showModal`/`showPopover` (`true` opens, `false` closes), `close`, `togglePopover`, `requestSubmit`, `checkValidity`, `reportValidity`, `showPicker`, `load`, `setSelectionRange`/`setRangeText`/`setPointerCapture`/`releasePointerCapture`/`fastSeek` (value = argument, array = argument list), …; a getter re-calls on change). `hideStrategy` is given through the `options` prop
(`options={{ hideStrategy: 'detach' }}`) or set on `motif.options.hideStrategy` in code; a bare
`hideStrategy="…"` attribute is not special (it becomes a DOM attribute / ordinary prop).
`action` on `form` and `formAction` / `formaction` on `button` / `input` take a URL or a submit handler
(`MotifFormAction`: `(data: FormData) => unknown` or `(sender, data) => unknown`); a function value is bound
to the submit event, a string is written as the attribute (`references/events-and-forms.md`).

---

<!-- references/pitfalls.md -->

# Pitfalls and known quirks

## React/Vue habits that break MotifJS code

| Wrong | Right | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `const [n, setN] = useState(0)` in a class | `state = reactive({ n: 0 })` | there is no `useState`; hooks are not the model |
| `useEffect(() => …, [])` | `onBuilt()` / `this.bindings.watch()`; `onMounted()` only when the element must be in the document | no render cycle; `onBuilt` may run before the element is attached |
| `onClick`, `className`, `htmlFor` | `onclick`, `class`, `for` | DOM names |
| `<div>{count}</div>` where `count` is a local | `<div>{state.count}</div>` or `{() => …}` | locals are frozen at build |
| `const { items } = this.state` then `{items.map()}` | `{this.state.items.map()}` | destructuring drops the proxy |
| `ref={(el: HTMLDivElement) => …}` | `ref={(c) => this.box = c}` then `c.element` | refs are components (on a plain DOM tag, the `Component` wrapping the element), never raw DOM nodes |
| `<a onclick:once:prevent={…}>` | one modifier per JSX attribute, or `this.motif.on('click:once:prevent', fn)` | JSX attribute names allow a single `:`; a chain is a parse error |
| `this.motif.setDisposable(this.context.on(…))` | just `this.context.on(…)` | subscriptions through `this.context` are already tied to the component |
| `key={index}` | `key={item.id}` | rows are matched by the item object, not by key; an index does not identify the item, so the duplicate-key check (`MJX202`) tells you nothing |
| `string[]` lists | `{ id, text }[]` | primitives lack identity |
| A row finds its item by id in a getter: `items.find((x) => x.id === props.id)` | hand the row the item (`<Row item={item}/>`), or a keyed `Map` in the store read with `byId(id)` | fine-grained tracking subscribes the row to every item's `id`: n rows → n² subscriptions, an id change reruns every row that scanned past it and a list replacement every row; `MJX004` at compile time, `MJX209` at run time |
| Returning arrays of JSX from helpers each render | Build once; mutate reactive data | there is no re-render |
| Cleanup in `componentWillUnmount` only | `this.motif.setDisposable(fn)` in the same place you create the resource | resources registered anywhere are disposed |
| `await nextTick(); expect(dom)` after `controls.add` | not needed; insertion is synchronous | but reactive *updates* flush on a microtask |
| `<Outlet/>`, `<Link to>` | `<RouterView/>`, `<a rel="router">` / `<RouterLink to el="a">` | |
| Forwarding `class`/`id`/`aria-*` from `this.props` to the root by hand | nothing — `<Card class="x" id="y"/>` falls through to the root automatically | only common attributes fall through (class/style/id/tabindex/role/aria-*/data-*); `title`, `disabled` and data props stay in `this.props`; `<div {...props}/>` on a DOM tag applies every key |

## Compiler quirks

1. **Block-arrow + local + conditional in child position**: `{() => { const x = …; return c ? <A/> : <B/>; }}` throws
   `ReferenceError: x is not defined` at runtime. Use expression-bodied arrows or a method.
2. **`class X extends Component` without a generic and without `super('tag')`** becomes a fragment;
   attributes written on the component tag are lost silently (DOM events on it listen on the content
   elements), and a wrapper returned from
   `view()` is a child, not the component's element. Declare `Component<HTMLDivElement>`. With an element
   declared, a wrapper returned from `view()` is a second element inside it (`<div><div>…</div></div>`):
   configure the component's own element in `onConfigured` and return only the content.
3. Only `.jsx .tsx .aio .mjsx .mtsx` are compiled as JSX; JSX inside `.ts` is not. In `.ts`/`.mts`/`.cts` files
   the plugin still injects `static elementTag` for a `Component<HTMLDivElement>` class, so the class has its own
   element there too.
4. `@Injectable` is a standard decorator; the Vite plugin lowers it in the JSX files it compiles and in
   `.ts`/`.mts`/`.cts`/`.js`/`.mjs`/`.cjs` files, not under `node_modules` or in `.d.ts` files; a `.ts`/`.js`
   file whose nearest tsconfig sets `experimentalDecorators: true` is left to esbuild's legacy transform. Only the
   registration is runtime: the decorator records the class when the module is evaluated and
   `builder.build()` registers it (see di.md).
5. **`childs` is a reserved name in child position.** `{this.childs}`, `{props.childs}`, `{childs}`
   compile to `controls.add(...)` (content slot), never to a text binding — the same is true for
   `{[compA, compB]}`. `{() => this.childs}` goes through a `Frame`, but `this.childs` is a plain
   array given once at setup: the getter re-runs only when a reactive value read inside changes, so
   assigning or pushing to `this.childs` does not swap the slot. Only an exact `childs` match is special: `{this.childsCount}` and
   `{this['childs']}` stay text bindings.
6. **`{a ?? b}` / `{a || b}`** compile to `bindings.method(() => a ?? b)`: left when present, otherwise
   right (the right side may be JSX); reactive. `{a && <X/>}` is `bindings.when`.
7. **`{this.method(x)}` (member call)** goes through `bindings.method`: a returned component is
   inserted (in a `Frame`, re-evaluated when reactive reads change), a string/number becomes reactive
   text; a boolean is text too (`false` prints `false`). The function runs once per change, and the result may switch between text and a component
   in place; `null` in place of a component empties the spot. `{helper(x)}` (plain identifier call) is inserted once, statically.
8. **`.map` on a non-identifier source** — `{[X].map(...)}`, `{(a ? xs : ys).map(...)}` — works
   (the source is wrapped in a getter). Named sources get a null-guard chain.
9. **SVG namespace**: every SVG tag (`g`, `path`, `circle`, …) is created with `createElementNS`,
   also when returned from a separate helper (`const icon = () => <g><path/></g>`). Tags that exist
   in both HTML and SVG (`a`, `title`, `style`, `script`) are SVG only under an `<svg>` ancestor in
   the same JSX tree; `<foreignObject>` switches back to HTML.
10. **Lowercase tag = local variable of the same name.** If a lowercase JSX tag matches a local
   variable/parameter in scope (`(content) => <div><content></content></div>`), the compiler inserts
   that variable as a component instead of creating an element. This is how `Virtualization`'s
   `mainTemplate` slot works; `{content}` there would be a text binding (`[object Object]`). Avoid
   naming locals after real HTML tags (`const div = ...`, `const input = ...`) inside components that
   render those tags.
11. **`x-style` equals `style`** (compiles to `sender.style(...)`, getter live). A style getter
   re-applies on change and clears keys it stops returning.
12. **`on:name` / `on-name` / `on_name` handlers follow the `motif.on` arity rule**: the handler is
   passed as is, so `fn.length <= 1` → `fn(event)`, otherwise `fn(sender, event)`. `fn.length` stops
   at the first default-valued or rest parameter: `(...a) => …` counts 0 and receives only the event.
   Only the prefix is stripped from the name: `on-my-event` → `my-event`, `on_my_event` → `my_event`.
13. **`ref={this.x}` / `ref={name}` is resolved by the compiler.** A method, a function-valued field
   or a local function is called with the component; a declared plain field or an uninitialised variable
   is assigned. When the compiler cannot tell (undeclared or inherited member, import, parameter,
   `props.x`, function-typed field, getter) the runtime calls it if it holds a function, else assigns.
   For an imported function the generated code still contains an assignment to the import: the dev
   server runs it, but `vite build` (Rollup) stops with "Illegal reassignment of import"; write
   `ref={(s) => importedFn(s)}`.

## Runtime quirks

- `const { params } = useNavigation()` keeps that moment's value; read `nav.params.id` inside a getter for live params. A hidden `keepAlive` page also re-runs route bindings with other routes' values.
- `app.onRouterChanged` is the only after-navigation hook. It fires on every navigation including the first
  and 404s, with `{ uri, params, meta, route, ok, initial, redirectedFrom?, direction, state }`; check `initial` to skip the first load.
- `redirect` fires only on the matched **leaf**: on a layout that has a `'/'` default child it never fires
  (the child is the leaf) — put the redirect on the default child.
- `params` never contains the `#fragment`, but it **does** merge query-string values with path params.
  Query values are strings like path params (`/users/5?page=2` → `{ id: '5', page: '2' }`), so
  `params.page === 2` is always false: convert explicitly (`Number(params.page)`). `true`, `null`, dates
  and JSON stay text too; a repeated key is an array of strings.
  If a query key has the same name as a path param, the path param wins. Query values come only from the
  navigated address: in `history` mode no `?` means no query params (the previous page's query never
  leaks); in `hash`/`file` mode the page query before `#` (`/?x=1#/a`) is used for routes without their own.
- A layout route must render `<RouterView/>` (and every named `<RouterView name>` its children target
  through `extend.targetOutlet`). Without it the child page is never mounted; dev mode warns `MJX301`
  (`RouterView outlet '…' was not built within 3000 ms`) — not an exception.
- `fallbacks.notFound` / `fallbacks.error`: the fallback renders inside the deepest layout whose
  path prefix matches the URL (the shell stays), the address bar is updated, `app.router.ok === false`.
- `keepAlive: true` keeps the instance: on leave it is detached from the outlet and cached
  (`onDeactivated`), on return it is re-attached in the same outlet position (`onActivated`); both
  propagate to the page's visible subtree.
  Cached instances live until `app.router.evict(nameOrRoute)` (no argument → all) or `app.dispose()`.
- `class.add(...)` works on SVG elements (`<svg class="ring">`).
- `x:mounted` / `onMounted` observers are released on dispose even if the element never attaches.
- A hidden or waiting component (list rows included) is replaced by a `<!--h-->` trace, so
  `element.parentNode` is `null` while hidden; with `hideStrategy: 'detach'` no trace is left either. `hideStrategy` is set through the `options` prop (`options={{ hideStrategy }}`) or `motif.options.hideStrategy` in code.
- `Virtualization` rows that scroll out of view are detached (not disposed) and kept in an LRU
  cache (`cacheSize`); `refresh()` disposes them all, while `setData()` and an `autoRefresh` reload
  dispose only the rows of items that are no longer in the data. Do not hold external references to
  row components across a `refresh()`. In jsdom, fake `clientHeight`/`scrollTop` or nothing renders.
- On a **plain DOM tag** any `on*` prop that is not a lifecycle name (`<div {...props}/>` with `onClick`,
  `new Component('div', { onclick })`) is registered as a DOM listener for the suffix event. On a
  component tag non-lifecycle `on*` props stay in `this.props` (the compiler wires known DOM event
  names written inline, see below).
- **The compiler warns you.** `@motifx/compiler` emits non-fatal build warnings with file, line and a
  code frame: `MJX001` (block-bodied arrow with parameters declaring locals then returning a conditional →
  `ReferenceError`), `MJX002` (camelCase DOM event name on a component tag — `<Comp onChange>` binds
  a DOM listener, not a callback prop; lowercase `<Button onclick>` is the deliberate spelling and is
  never warned), `MJX003` (`.map()` item without `key`; rows are matched by the item object, so the key only feeds the
  `MJX202` duplicate check), `MJX004` (a reactive getter looks an item up by scanning a reactive list with
  `find`/`findIndex`/`some`/`every` and an `x.field === value` predicate: n components → n² reads per change; use a keyed
  map or `untracked`), `MJX017` (a reactive getter writes a reactive value it also reads; it retriggers itself), `MJX018`
  (`sort`/`reverse` on a reactive list inside a getter, or `push`/… when the getter also reads the list; sort a copy), `MJX007` (unknown `x-*` name; it is passed on
  as an `on<name>` prop), `MJX015` (a class component override of `build`/`dispose`/`style`/… that
  can finish without reaching `super`; checked in `.ts`/`.js` files too), `MJX016` (a `switch` or
  `return a ? b : c` getter the compiler cannot lower — non-literal `case` label, `return` or JSX before the
  `switch`, `break` leaving it — runs as `bindings.method`: no branch is kept). Disable with
  `compiler({ diagnostics: false })`. A separate type-aware check, `npx motif-lint`,
  reports `MJX005`: a ternary on a component prop whose declared type is not `Bind<T>` (the compiler
  cannot see prop types; TypeScript does not see the getter wrapping). A hit is a real contract
  violation.
- **Some JSX fails the build.** `x-reload`, `x-bind`, `x-effect`, `x-focus`, `x-interrupt`, `x-to`,
  `x-list`, `x-loop` are not directives (`MJX006`); use `x-wait`/`x-display`, `{items.map(i => <X key={i.id}/>)}`,
  `effect(...)` or `ref` + `focus()` instead. A `function () {}` child is `MJX008` (write `{() => …}`).
  A string/boolean event handler (`onclick="go()"`) is `MJX009`; invalid lifecycle/directive values and
  unsupported tag or child forms are `MJX010`–`MJX013`.
  The thrown error carries the code in `error.code`.
- **Runtime messages are coded too.** Thrown framework errors are `MotifError` (`code`, message
  `[motifjs] MJX302: …`); errors the framework catches and reports (component and route hooks incl. rejected async hooks `MJX122`/`MJX306`, guards `MJX306` which cancel the navigation, event handlers and application event listeners incl. `onRouterChanged` `MJX123`, effects `MJX208`, dispose and data-load failures)
  reach `errorHandler.addListener(fn)` as `MotifError` with the original error in `cause`; warnings print
  only in development. These coded reports do not go to `setUnexpectedErrorHandler`.
- A lifecycle listener added in code with `this.motif.on('x:built', fn)` (likewise `x:configured`,
  `x:disposed`, `x:mounted` and the other `x:` names) that throws is reported as `MJX122`
  (`The component x:built hook threw.`), the same as the hook written as a method or a JSX prop. A
  throwing `ref` callback on a plain tag or a class component tag is `MJX122` too; the component is
  still created.
- **Not sure what a `{…}` compiles to? Ask the compiler:** `npx motif-explain file.tsx` prints,
