  per expression, the real lowered call, its reactivity class (`LIVE`/`STATIC`/`ONCE`/`RECEIVER`/`RUNTIME`) and its dependency surface. Two facts it makes visible that people miss:
  `attr={f(x)}` on a DOM tag is evaluated ONCE (write `attr={() => f(x)}` to keep it live), and
  `prop={object}` on a component passes the value once (a reactive proxy stays live only if the
  receiver reads its fields inside a getter).
- **A ternary in attribute/prop position is ALWAYS wrapped lazily** (`mode={x ? 'a' : 'b'}` →
  `mode: () => x ? 'a' : 'b'`), on DOM tags and component tags alike. This is deliberate: without it
  the expression would be evaluated once during `view()` and freeze. The contract is that the
  receiving component declares the prop as `Bind<T>` and reads it through `read()` / `toGetter()`.
  A component that declares a plain type and uses the prop directly is the thing that is wrong (an
  `Icon` reading `name` directly gets `() => …` and draws its fallback glyph); fix the receiver, not
  the call site. Every other expression form passes by value.
- A valueless attribute on a component tag (`<Comp flag />`) passes `flag: true`. Member-expression
  tags (`<Foo.Bar/>`) compile like any other component tag.
- **Do not shadow `ComponentBase` members.** Reserved on a class component: `build`, `dispose`,
  `disposeAsync`, `style`, `setText`, `setState`, `reState`, `using`, `doWork`, `getService`,
  `useModel`, `$`, `context`, `siblings`, `serviceProvider`, `isWait`, `element`, `props`,
  `controls`, `class`, `attr`, `bindings`, `motif`, `parent`, `childs` and the `is…` state flags
  (`isBuilt`, `isVisible` …). `view()`, the lifecycle hooks, `initializeComponent` and
  `onElementCreating` are meant to be written; an override of `build`/`dispose`/`style` … calls
  `super.<name>(...)`. TypeScript reports only clearly incompatible types (`style = 'red'`); it
  misses `any` fields, compatible-signature methods (`build() {}` leaves the component empty, a
  page's `dispose()` without `super` is never torn down on navigation, a parameterless `style()`
  drops the tag's `style`). The accessors `motif`, `controls`, `class`, `attr`, `bindings`,
  `context`, `siblings`, `serviceProvider`, `isWait` and the `is…` flags cannot be redeclared as a field
  (`declare` included): TS2610. An overridden `dispose()` runs only when that component's own `dispose()`
  is called (by hand, `controls.remove`, `controls.clear`); a component disposed together with its parent
  does not get the call, only `onDisposing`/`onDisposed` and `motif.setDisposable(...)` registrations run,
  so put teardown there. The compiler warns `MJX015` at build time for an
  override that skips `super` on any path (`if (x) return;`, one-branch `if`, loop, `catch`,
  callback), in `.ts`/`.js` files too; only `if (this.isBuilt|isDisposed|isWait) return;` in
  `build` and `if (this.isDisposed) return;` in `dispose` are exempt. In development mode `MJX128` reports, once per class,
  an override without `super`, an instance field hiding a method/accessor, and a replaced
  `controls`/`attr`/`class`/`bindings`/`motif`/`element`/`parent`; `props` and the flags are not
  checked. The framework operations `show`, `hide`, `toggle`, `on`, `off`, `trigger`, `addHandler`,
  `clear`, `register`, `setDisposable`, `stopAnimations` and `options` live on `this.motif`, so a
  subclass may use those names for its own members.
- **A page that puts thousands of children into one element in a single update freezes until all of
  them are built.** Write `x-chunk` on that element: the first 100 build at once and the rest over
  the next frames, each frame sized to stay near 50 ms, `.map` rows created only on their turn;
  `Virtualization` keeps only the visible rows in the DOM and is the tool past a few tens of thousands
  of rows. Nothing changes for elements without the directive.
- **Reach for `x-wait`/`x-display` before `{cond && <X/>}`.** The directive keeps the instance and
  swaps a `<!--h-->` placeholder, and when the condition starts hidden the element is never built at
  all (subtree included; `view()` and the build hooks wait, while a class still runs its constructor and
  config hooks). `{cond && <X/>}` constructs a new instance on every
  show and disposes it on every hide — correct only when that churn is what you want. `&&` and
  ternary branches are rebuilt only when the condition value changes, so a plain-expression component
  prop inside a branch (`<Badge count={state.n}/>`) is a snapshot; pass `count={() => state.n}` and
  read it as `Bind<T>`. A single element
  whose class/text is a getter is the cheapest for mutually exclusive one-liners. Consecutive
  `x-display` siblings under one parent are safe.
- Directives and lifecycle props written on a **function component** tag (`<InfoBar x-display={...} />`,
  `onBuilt`, `x-mounted`, `x-initializing` and the other lifecycle spellings, `initializeComponent`, `ref`) are applied to the root the function returns — the function does not
  forward anything. Class components receive them in the constructor.
- **Short-circuit inside a reactive getter loses dependencies.** `arr.some(...)`, `every`, `a || b` stop
  reading once the answer is known, so the binding never subscribes to the rest. Loop over everything
  and accumulate instead.
- **A class with `#private` fields does not survive `reactive()`.** Getters and methods called through
  the proxy get the proxy as `this`, so one that touches a `#private` field throws `TypeError`, whether the
  instance is wrapped directly or stored in a reactive field. Keep such an instance out of reactive state
  and hold its reactive data in a `reactive({ … })` field; a TypeScript `private` field is an ordinary
  field and works.
- **`untracked(fn)`** reads without creating dependencies — use it when an effect
  writes to a store it also reads, or when a debounced async effect must consult sync state.
- **Template/slot props** (`<Card headerTemplate={<h1/>}/>` read as `{props.headerTemplate}`) work
  directly — no `{() => ...}` needed and no component-vs-data annotation. But the placement is decided
  once, in the parent's `initializeComponent`, and props are a plain object taken then: a template that is
  `null` at that time and assigned later reaches neither the direct form (it writes nothing and warns
  `MJX204`) nor `{() => props.headerTemplate}` (nothing reactive is read inside). The parent passes a
  template that changes through a ternary or a getter, and the child declares it `Bind<ComponentBase | null>`
  and reads it with `{() => read(props.headerTemplate)}` (a `Frame` slot).
- A component callback prop whose name matches a **known DOM event** (`onChange`, `onInput`, `onSelect`,
  `onToggle`, `onResize`, `onSearch`…) is consumed as that DOM listener and does **not** reach `this.props`.
  A name the compiler does not know as a DOM event (`onmouseenter`, `onpointerdown`, `onfocusin`,
  `ontransitionend`) is the opposite: no listener, the value stays a prop without a warning; listen with
  `on:mouseenter={…}`. Name callbacks after
  domain events instead: `onValueChange`, `onAdd`, `onDismiss`.
- `Application.CreateBuilder()` may be called once per page; a second call while an app is running throws
  `MJX405` (it is allowed once `app.dispose()` has been called, even without `await`). Call `rebuild()` for
  hot-reload scenarios. `app.dispose()` disposes the services last, after the tree and its leave animations,
  so every `onDisposing` / `onDisposed` and code running during an animation still sees services and `context`.
- `this.context.on(...)` returns an unsubscribe function and is removed automatically when the component
  is disposed (so is `this.context.onRouterChanged`). `this.context.onLifecycle(...)`,
  `Application.main.on(...)` and a captured `app.on(...)` are not: keep and call (or
  `motif.setDisposable`) their unsubscribe.
- Raw `effect()` outside components never stops by itself.
- **An effect must not write a value it also reads.** `state.n++` inside an effect is a read *and* a
  write, so the effect retriggers itself; so does `list.sort()`, which reads and writes the array in place.
  Wrap bookkeeping writes (counters, logs) and in-place sorts in `untracked(...)`, or sort a copy.
  The framework bounds this: an effect that runs 50 times in one flush is skipped for the rest of that
  flush and an `MJX203` dev warning names it; other queued effects are unaffected.
- **Chained state settles in the same microtask.** Effect A writing state that effect B reads is
  supported; the final state does not depend on creation order and one `await tick()` is enough. An effect
  that also reads such a value can run twice in that microtask, and its first run may see the old value.
- An effect that throws does not abort the rest of the flush; the error is reported as `MJX208` and reaches
  `errorHandler.addListener(fn)` as `MotifError` (original error in `cause`). The throwing run has no value:
  `effect(getter, onValue)` does not call `onValue`, and a `when`/`ternary`/`switchCase` branch keeps its content.
- `scoped` services: one instance per navigation (everything the navigation puts on screen, constructor
  injection included, shares it; callers hold a handle that follows the current navigation); without a
  router there is one instance on the root provider, disposed with `app.provider.dispose()`. See di.md.
- SSR is not supported; it has not been planned yet and may be considered later. Importing `@motifx/core` works without a DOM, but creating any element
  throws `MJX101` when no `document` exists.

## Diagnosing "it does not update"

1. Is the value read **inside** a getter or directly as `state.field` in JSX? (`{label}` is static.)
2. Is the object actually a `reactive()` proxy (not a destructured copy or a class field assigned before proxying)?
3. Are the list items objects (rows follow the item object, not `key`)? Are you mutating the proxied array (`state.items.push`) rather than a stale reference?
4. Did an `untracked` or `peek()` wrap the read?
5. Was the component disposed (`isDisposed`) before the async result arrived? Use `doWork`/`using`.

---

<!-- references/reporting-bugs.md -->

# Reporting a MotifJS bug

When something you see contradicts this skill, the docs at https://motifjs.com or the type
declarations, and a minimal reproduction shows the cause is MotifJS rather than the app, offer
to report it. Never file anything without the user's yes.

## 1. Make sure it is a MotifJS bug

Go through this list before you say "bug":

- **Reproduce it outside the app.** Write the smallest component that shows the behavior: one
  file, one component, no services or router unless the bug needs them. If the small version
  works, the cause is in the app; keep looking there.
- **Rule out JavaScript itself.** A plain value is read once: `note={editor.selected}` does not
  follow later changes, `note={() => editor.selected}` with a `Bind<T>` prop and `read()` does.
  A destructured reactive field is a copy. These are not bugs (`references/pitfalls.md`).
- **Rule out the documented quirks.** Check `references/pitfalls.md` and the reference file for
  the area. A behavior the skill already describes is not a bug, even when it surprises you.
- **Check the versions.** `npm ls @motifx/core @motifx/compiler`. The two packages are always
  released with the same version number; a mismatch prints `MJX121` in development mode.
- **Turn development mode on.** `app.useDevelopment(true)` before `app.run(...)` prints the `MJX`
  warnings. A correct warning (for example `MJX202` for a duplicate key) is the framework doing
  its job.
- **Find the layer.** `npx motif-explain file.tsx` prints what the compiler made of each JSX
  expression. Wrong output there is a compiler bug (`@motifx/compiler`); correct output with
  wrong behavior at runtime is a core bug (`@motifx/core`). For a view written without JSX it is
  always the core.

## 2. Ask the user

Tell the user in one or two sentences, in their language, what is wrong and how you confirmed
it, then ask whether they want it reported. Offer only the options that exist:

- give them the filled issue text to post themselves,
- file it yourself (only when you can, see step 5),
- leave it.

If they say no, do not ask again for the same problem in the session.

## 3. Write the reproduction

The reproduction in the issue is **made up**. Never paste the user's code, names, URLs, data,
tokens, file paths or business rules. Rebuild the behavior with neutral names (`Item`, `List`,
`state.items`, `/api/items`) in the smallest code that still fails, and run it once to confirm
it shows the bug. Give it in the style the bug appears in (class, function or Options; JSX or
not; TypeScript or JavaScript) and say which styles you tried.

## 4. Fill the template

Write the issue in English. Pick the repository by layer:

| The problem is in | Repository |
|---|---|
| `@motifx/core` or `@motifx/compiler` (runtime, compiler, `motif-lint`, `motif-explain`) | `motifjsdev/motifjs` |
| this skill told you something wrong | `motifjs-community/skills` |

```markdown
**Title:** [core|compiler] <what goes wrong> when <condition>

### Versions
- @motifx/core: <version>
- @motifx/compiler: <version>
- Bundler: <Vite x.y | Rollup x.y | none (UMD)>
- TypeScript: <version or "JavaScript">
- Runtime: <browser and version | Node version + jsdom>
- OS: <name>

### Component style
<class | function | Options>, <JSX | without JSX>, <TypeScript | JavaScript>.
Also tried: <other styles and whether they fail>

### What happens
<one paragraph: the wrong behavior, plainly>

### Reproduction
<every file needed, each in its own fenced block with its path>

### Steps
1. ...
2. ...

### Expected
<what should happen, and where the docs or types say so (link)>

### Actual
<what happens instead>

### Console
<MJX codes, warnings and stack traces, verbatim; "nothing" if silent>

### Compiled output (compiler bugs only)
<the relevant `npx motif-explain` lines>

### Workaround
<what avoids it, or "none found">
```

### A filled example

The bug below is invented. It only shows the level of detail an issue needs.

````markdown
**Title:** [core] `x-display` stops reacting after the component is detached and added back

### Versions
- @motifx/core: 1.2.0
- @motifx/compiler: 1.2.0
- Bundler: Vite 6.3.5
- TypeScript: 5.6.3
- Runtime: Chrome 141
- OS: Windows 11

### Component style
Class, JSX, TypeScript.
Also tried: function component with JSX (fails the same way), class without JSX using
`preconfig: (p) => p.bindings.display(...)` (fails the same way).

### What happens
A component whose element is shown with `x-display` keeps reacting while it stays in place. After
`controls.detach` and `controls.add` put it back in the same parent, changing the condition no
longer hides or shows the element. Text bindings inside it still update.

### Reproduction

`src/Details.tsx`
```tsx
import { Component, reactive } from "@motifx/core";

export class Details extends Component<HTMLDivElement> {
  state = reactive({ open: true, label: "Shipping details" });

  override view() {
    return <p x-display={() => this.state.open}>{() => this.state.label}</p>;
  }
}
```

`src/main.ts`
```ts
import { Application, Component } from "@motifx/core";
import { Details } from "./Details";

const app = Application.CreateBuilder().build();
app.useDevelopment(true);
const page = new Component("main");
app.run("#app", page);

const details = new Details();
page.controls.add(details);

page.controls.detach(details).then(() => {
  page.controls.add(details);
  details.state.open = false;
  details.state.label = "Billing details";
});
```

### Steps
1. Run the reproduction with `npm run dev`.
2. Look at the `<p>` inside `main` once the page has loaded.

### Expected
The `<p>` is hidden and a `<!--h-->` trace stands in its place; a detached component keeps its
bindings when it is added again (https://motifjs.com/en/docs/lifecycle).

### Actual
The `<p>` stays visible and reads "Billing details": the text binding works, the display binding
does not. Setting `open` back to `true` and to `false` again changes nothing.

### Console
Nothing. No `MJX` warning in development mode.

### Workaround
Create a new `Details` instead of adding the detached one back.
````

## 5. File it or hand it over

- **Look for duplicates first.** With the GitHub CLI:
  `gh issue list --repo motifjsdev/motifjs --state all --search "<two or three keywords>"`.
  Without it, give the user the search link
  `https://github.com/motifjsdev/motifjs/issues?q=<keywords>`. If an open issue matches, offer to
  add the new details to it instead.
- **Show the final title and body to the user** and wait for their yes, even when they already
  agreed to a report in step 2.
- **You can file it yourself only when a tool for it is there and authorized:** `gh auth status`
  succeeds, or a GitHub tool is connected in this session. Then:
  `gh issue create --repo motifjsdev/motifjs --title "<title>" --body-file issue.md`.
  Do not add labels or assignees. Give the user the link to the new issue.
- **Otherwise hand it over:** give the user the title and the body as a Markdown block and the
  link `https://github.com/motifjsdev/motifjs/issues/new` (or
  `https://github.com/motifjs-community/skills/issues/new` for the skill).
